1.explanation: 1) lighthouse-core/gather/computed/critical-request-chains.js: This is where the extractChain() algorithm selects any finished, “High” priority record and walks its initiator chain. No check excludes resourceType ‘iframe’ or URL schemes like data:, so those nodes end up in the CRC tree even though they aren’t render-blocking. 2) lighthouse-core/audits/critical-request-chains.js: The audit simply invokes the computed artifact from above and emits the unfiltered tree as its details. Since the computed artifact includes iframes/data URIs, the audit reports them as critical. 3) lighthouse-core/report/v2/renderer/crc-details-renderer.js: This file renders the raw CRC JSON into the interactive tree in the final report. It doesn’t filter out any node types, so you see the iframe and its children exactly as they were passed in. All three files participate in collecting, auditing, and displaying iframe and data-URI requests as if they were critical.
1.bug_scenario: When Lighthouse computes its Critical Request Chains (CRC), it considers any resource with “High” priority as render-blocking—even if it’s an <iframe> or a data URI. In the reproducer you stand up three mock network records (a main document, an iframe document, and a stylesheet inside that iframe) all marked High priority. Calling CriticalRequestChains.extractChain yields a tree that includes the iframe node and its CSS child as “critical,” exactly like the screenshot from PaulIrish.com. Since iframes (and data: URIs) do not block rendering, they shouldn’t appear in the CRC tree.

2.explanation:
• lighthouse-core/gather/computed/critical-request-chains.js is the core logic that walks the list of networkRecords and builds the CRC tree. It currently treats any record with high priority (including iframes and data URIs) as critical. To fix the bug we need to exclude records whose resourceType.category is 'iframe' (and their descendants) and requests whose URL starts with 'data:'.

• lighthouse-core/audits/critical-request-chains.js invokes the computed artifact and shapes the audit’s output. While it doesn’t build the chain itself, it defines what gets reported; updating it ensures that any top-level filtering of frames/data URIs carries through into the final audit result.

• lighthouse-core/report/v2/renderer/crc-details-renderer.js is responsible for rendering the tree in the report UI. Even after computed filtering, the renderer must gracefully handle the absence of iframe or data-uri nodes (and avoid any hard assumptions about their presence). Adjustments here will prevent visual artifacts or errors when those nodes are omitted.
2.bug_scenario: When you run CriticalRequestChains.extractChain on a set of network records that include an <iframe> document (and its children), the iframe and its sub-resources end up in the “critical” request chain even though iframes aren’t render-blocking. Likewise, data URIs (which aren’t real network requests from CRC’s perspective) still show up as leaf nodes in the CRC tree. Both behaviors lead to an inflated or misleading critical-chain graph.
